name: Gigabit Infrastructure Act
evidence_rating: ex-ante only: applied from Nov 2025; only implementation tracking
summary: The Commission forecast that the Act would cut the cost of building fibre and 5G networks by EUR 14.5 billion and reduce the public subsidies needed by EUR 2.4 billion, mainly through re-using ducts and poles and faster permits. Its main rules have only applied since November 2025, and by March 2026 about half of EU countries had started adapting national law. No evidence yet shows whether costs have fallen.

indicators.objective: The proposal has no LFS indicators; the memorandum foresees a report five years after entry into force, based on indicators and a data-collection mechanism to be drawn up by the Communications Committee

indicators.indicator: Reduction in cost of network deployment to 2030
indicators.evidence: Main provisions applied from 12 Nov 2025; not evaluated.

indicators.indicator: New network km deployed by re-using physical infrastructure or coordinating civil works
Administrative cost savings for operators; digital permit procedures
indicators.target_or_baseline: EUR 40m a year for operators; EUR 3-4m a year for local authorities
indicators.evidence: About half of Member States had begun adopting implementing measures by March 2026, with divergent approaches to tacit approval of permits.

indicators.objective: Contribute to Digital Decade gigabit targets
indicators.evidence: Coverage tracked in Digital Decade reports but not attributed to the GIA.

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), Impact Assessment accompanying the Gigabit Infrastructure Act proposal (executive summary SWD(2023) 47), SWD(2023) 46
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the Gigabit Infrastructure Act proposal (executive summary SWD(2023) 47)
literature.outcomes: deployment costs; subsidies; admin costs; emissions
literature.headline: Deployment costs EUR 14.5bn lower and public subsidies EUR 2.4bn lower; 470,000 km of network via re-use (vs 250,000 km); one-off costs EUR 70m; operator admin savings EUR 40m a year; 0.7 Mt GHG avoided to 2030
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected the Act to cut the cost of rolling out fibre and 5G by EUR 14.5 billion and save EUR 2.4 billion of public subsidies.

literature.citation: Cullen International (2026), National implementation of the EU Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Cullen International benchmark (March 2026)
literature.title: National implementation of the EU Gigabit Infrastructure Act
literature.headline: Main provisions applied from 12 Nov 2025; about half of Member States had begun adopting implementing legislation; approaches diverge on tacit approval, access to private buildings and fibre-ready labels
literature.summary_plain: A March 2026 survey found only about half of EU countries had started adapting national law, with different approaches to automatic permit approval.
literature.interested_party: Commercial regulatory-intelligence firm whose clients include telecom operators

literature.authors: Ilsa Godlovitch, Peter Kroon, Sonia Strube Martins, Saskja Schaefer, Stefano Lucidi, Nico Steffen, Thomas Plueckebaum, Cara Schwarz-Schilling (WIK-Consult); Facundo Herrera, Ricardas Juskevicius (ICF)
literature.title: Support Study associated with the Review of the Broadband Cost Reduction Directive: Evaluation Report
literature.venue: Study for the European Commission, DG CNECT (Publications Office, doi:10.2759/560564)
literature.method: ex-post evaluation of the predecessor Directive 2014/61/EU: stakeholder survey, 56 structured interviews, case studies in 12 Member States, desk research
literature.outcomes: network roll-out enabled, cost savings from infrastructure access, use of permit and transparency measures
literature.headline: Where effectively applied, the Broadband Cost Reduction Directive (replaced by the GIA) contributed at least 100,000 km of additional network roll-out in 2016-2020, and operators benefiting from access to physical infrastructure reported 10-30% cost savings, though application varied widely across provisions and countries.
literature.summary_plain: Before the Gigabit Infrastructure Act replaced it, the earlier EU law on cheaper broadband roll-out was evaluated. It helped build extra network where countries applied it properly, but results were uneven, which shaped the new Act.
literature.quality: Predecessor-provision evaluation (GIA repeals and extends Directive 2014/61/EU); survey and case evidence, no counterfactual; figures partly from interested operators.
literature.interested_party: Commissioned by the European Commission; cost-saving figures self-reported by telecom operators
literature.citation: Ilsa Godlovitch, Peter Kroon, Sonia Strube Martins, Saskja Schaefer, Stefano Lucidi, Nico Steffen, Thomas Plueckebaum, Cara Schwarz-Schilling (WIK-Consult); Facundo Herrera, Ricardas Juskevicius (ICF) (2023), Support Study associated with the Review of the Broadband Cost Reduction Directive: Evaluation Report, Study for the European Commission, DG CNECT (Publications Office, doi:10.2759/560564)
